subsystems.name: Chassis organisms
subsystems.role: the microbes that do the chemistry; often two or more species or strains that split the job.
parts: bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas putida or Clostridium species
yeasts such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae or Yarrowia lipolytica

subsystems.name: Metabolic modules
subsystems.role: each organism carries only part of the pathway, so no single cell bears the whole metabolic burden.

subsystems.name: Control and communication circuits
subsystems.role: keep the members in the right proportions and stop one from overgrowing the others.

subsystems.name: Culture environment
subsystems.role: the vessel, feed and physical conditions that keep the community alive.

subsystems.name: Measurement and modelling
subsystems.role: tells the designer who is winning and why.

subsystems.name: Containment and downstream processing
subsystems.role: stops the organisms escaping and separates the product from a mixed broth.
parts: physical containment and waste kill steps

buildSteps.title: Choose the product and pathway
buildSteps.detail: Define the target molecule and map a biosynthetic route to it, usually borrowing enzymes from plants, fungi or other microbes.

buildSteps.title: Split the pathway
buildSteps.detail: Decide which steps go in which organism — for example, one strain breaks down a complex feedstock while a second converts the released sugars into the product.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the strains
buildSteps.detail: Genes are assembled and inserted using CRISPR or older recombination methods, then screened for productivity.

buildSteps.title: Wire in dependencies
buildSteps.detail: Amino-acid auxotrophies, cross-fed metabolites or quorum-sensing circuits are added so the partners need each other and stay balanced.

buildSteps.title: Test small
buildSteps.detail: Strains are grown together in microplates and chemostats to see whether the community is stable and whether it beats a single strain.

buildSteps.title: Optimise the consortium
buildSteps.detail: Feeding rates, inoculation ratios and oxygen levels are tuned, guided by sequencing and metabolic measurements.

buildSteps.title: Scale to bioreactors
buildSteps.detail: The mix is run in litres to cubic metres, where mixing, oxygen transfer and contamination become the hard problems.

buildSteps.title: Recover the product
buildSteps.detail: Cells are separated and the compound is purified, while containment measures are verified.

prerequisites.why: introducing and tuning many pathway genes across several organisms depends on it.
they predict which divisions of labour will actually work, but community models remain less reliable than single-cell ones.
releasing engineered organisms, or letting them escape a plant, is unacceptable without reliable kill switches.
cost competitiveness depends on running continuously on waste or gas streams rather than pure sugars.
you cannot control a consortium you cannot measure — sequencing and flow cytometry make composition visible.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale co-cultures that outperform single strains for some molecules
pathway.unlocks: proof that dividing a pathway reduces metabolic burden and expands the usable feedstock range.

pathway.milestone: stable consortia running in pilot bioreactors on lignocellulose, syngas or waste streams
pathway.unlocks: biomanufacturing that does not compete with food crops for sugar.

pathway.milestone: plug-and-play module libraries and standardised community design tools
pathway.unlocks: faster development, so new molecules need months rather than years.

pathway.milestone: self-regulating continuous communities integrated with downstream processing
pathway.unlocks: chemical and fuel production that is genuinely cost-competitive with petrochemical routes.
